section_heading: Understand the causes of layout shifts

supports.section: Understand the causes of layout shifts
supports.excerpt:
The live metrics view of the Performance Panel allows monitoring of a web page's CLS score while interacting with the page.

As an alternative to using the DevTools, you can browse your web page while recording layout shifts using a Performance Observer pasted into the console.

For more information, see Debug layout shifts.

After you've identified any common causes of CLS, the timespans user flow mode of Lighthouse can also be used to ensure typical user flows don't regress by introducing layout shifts.

The `web-vitals` library has attribution functions that let you collect this additional information. For more information, see Debug performance in the field. Other RUM providers have also started collecting and presenting this data similarly.

skill_drafts.name: Monitor CLS Score in Real-Time
skill_drafts.description: Use the Performance Panel's live metrics view to observe cumulative layout shift (CLS) scores while interacting with a web page, identifying when and where shifts occur during user sessions.
applicable_signals: Page interaction triggers visible layout shifts
CLS score increases during user actions
Visual instability observed during development testing
contraindications: When DevTools access is unavailable or disabled
When real-time observation is not feasible
intervention_moves: Interact with page elements (scroll, click, type)
Observe CLS metric updates and shift events
triggers: Need to observe layout shifts as they happen during page interaction
Debugging visual instability in a live page session
constraints: Does not capture field user data
Dependent on browser and page state
cautions: Live metrics reflect only current session; not representative of all users
DevTools overhead may affect page performance
Requires active interaction to observe shifts
output_contract: Live CLS metric displayed in Performance Panel showing shift events and cumulative score during page interaction. Output includes timing of shifts and identification of elements causing layout changes.

metadata.prompt: Open the Performance Panel in your browser DevTools. Navigate to the live metrics view. Interact with the web page (scroll, click, type) while observing the CLS score update in real-time. Note the timing and elements associated with each layout shift event.

skill_drafts.name: Record Layout Shifts via Performance Observer
skill_drafts.description: Paste a Performance Observer script into the browser console to capture and log layout shift events on a web page. Provides a programmatic alternative to DevTools for detecting and analyzing Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) during page interaction.
applicable_signals: Need to capture layout shift data without DevTools
Automating CLS detection in custom test scripts
Debugging layout shifts during page interaction
contraindications: DevTools Performance Panel is sufficient for one-off analysis
Measuring CLS at scale in production (use RUM libraries instead)
Real-time visual monitoring of layout shifts is the primary need
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Open the browser console on the target web page'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Paste a Performance Observer script configured to observe layout-shift entries'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Interact with the page or allow it to load fully'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Review console output for recorded layout shift events with timing and attribution data'}
triggers: You need to capture layout shift data without relying on DevTools; automating CLS detection in custom test scripts.
constraints: Script must be pasted into console while page is loaded or during interaction
Output is limited to console log; not suitable for persistent data collection without additional logging infrastructure
cautions: Console output may be cleared or lost if page reloads
Performance Observer API support varies by browser; verify browser compatibility
For production-scale CLS collection, use dedicated RUM providers or the web-vitals library instead
output_contract: Console output or log containing recorded layout shift events, including timing information and attribution data for each shift. Output is available in the browser console and can be copied or exported for analysis.

metadata.prompt: Use this skill when you need to programmatically capture layout shift data without relying on the DevTools Performance Panel. Paste a Performance Observer script into the browser console while browsing the target page. The observer will record layout shift events with timing and attribution details, outputting results to the console log. This approach is useful for automating CLS detection in custom test scripts or when DevTools is not available.

skill_drafts.name: Validate User Flows Against CLS Regression
skill_drafts.description: Use Lighthouse's timespans user flow mode to test typical user interaction flows and ensure they do not introduce new layout shifts, preventing CLS regressions.
skill_drafts.objective: CLS regression prevention in user flows
applicable_signals: User flows are defined and reproducible
Baseline CLS metrics are available for comparison
contraindications: Performing initial CLS diagnosis or root cause analysis
Measuring field performance at scale (use RUM providers instead)
Lighthouse is not available or cannot be integrated into the testing environment
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Define representative user flows', 'detail': 'Identify typical user interactions (e.g., page load, button click, form submission, navigation) that should be tested.'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Configure Lighthouse timespans mode', 'detail': 'Set up Lighthouse to run in user flow mode with timespans covering your defined interactions.'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Execute the flow test', 'detail': 'Run Lighthouse on the target page or application, allowing it to record layout shifts throughout the user flow.'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Inspect CLS metrics in the report', 'detail': 'Review the Lighthouse report for CLS values, shift sources, and any elements contributing to layout instability.'}
{'step': 5, 'action': 'Compare against baseline', 'detail': 'Check if CLS metrics have regressed compared to the previous baseline or acceptable threshold.'}
{'step': 6, 'action': 'Document findings and remediate if needed', 'detail': 'Record results; if regressions are detected, identify the shift sources and plan fixes.'}
triggers: After identifying common CLS causes and before deploying changes
When validating typical user interaction flows in CI/CD pipelines
Before releasing updates that may affect page layout stability
constraints: Requires Lighthouse to be installed and executable
User flows must be clearly defined and reproducible
Baseline CLS metrics must be established for regression detection
cautions: Lab measurements may not reflect real-world field conditions; use field data for validation
Timespans mode requires explicit flow definition; incomplete flows may miss regressions
CLS thresholds should be set based on business requirements and user experience goals
output_contract: Lighthouse report showing user flow timespans with CLS metrics confirming no regression or identifying new shift sources. Output includes: CLS score for the flow, list of elements causing shifts, and comparison to baseline.

metadata.prompt: Execute Lighthouse in timespans user flow mode on your web application. Define representative user flows (e.g., page load → interaction → navigation). Run the flow and inspect the CLS metrics in the resulting report. Confirm that CLS values remain within acceptable thresholds and identify any new shift sources if regressions are detected.

skill_drafts.name: Collect Field CLS Attribution Data
skill_drafts.description: Use the web-vitals library's attribution functions or RUM provider APIs to gather detailed Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) information from real users in production, including which elements caused shifts and when they occurred.
skill_drafts.objective: Production CLS data collection and attribution
applicable_signals: RUM infrastructure or web-vitals library integration possible
Need for attribution-level CLS insights beyond lab measurements
contraindications: Performing lab-based diagnosis using DevTools or Lighthouse
Testing in development or staging environments without production traffic
RUM infrastructure not available or not deployable
Privacy constraints preventing collection of user interaction data
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Integrate web-vitals library or RUM provider with attribution support into production application'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Configure attribution functions to capture element identifiers and timing information for each layout shift'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Collect CLS metrics along with user context (session ID, user segment, page type) from production sessions'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Aggregate collected data in your analytics or monitoring backend'}
{'step': 5, 'action': 'Analyze patterns to identify which elements and scenarios cause the most significant layout shifts'}
triggers: Need to understand CLS patterns in production environments
Correlating layout shifts with real user behavior and interactions
Debugging field performance issues reported by end users
Establishing baseline CLS metrics across user segments
constraints: Requires web-vitals library or compatible RUM provider with attribution support
Data collection must comply with privacy and consent policies
Attribution data collection adds minimal overhead to user sessions
cautions: Ensure user consent and privacy compliance before collecting field data
Monitor instrumentation overhead to avoid impacting page performance
Aggregate data appropriately to protect individual user privacy
output_contract: Collected field CLS metrics with attribution data including element identifiers, shift timing, and user context aggregated from production sessions; ready for analysis and correlation with user behavior patterns.

metadata.prompt: Instrument your production application with the web-vitals library's attribution functions or equivalent RUM provider APIs to collect CLS metrics from real user sessions. Capture element identifiers, shift timing, and user context. Aggregate and analyze the collected data to identify patterns in layout shift causes and frequency across your user base.
